claims.text: Exactly one of the five outcomes, plus why.
claims.why: The five outcomes are not defined in this chunk; the docstring refers to them but they are not present.

claims.text: True only for ``fixed``. Nothing else is a pass, including ``could_not_run`` -- especially ``could_not_run``.
claims.why: The property returns self.outcome == OUTCOME_FIXED. OUTCOME_FIXED is not defined in this chunk but the property logic matches the claim.

claims.text: Pure: ``(outcome, reason, fixed, unfixed, regressed)`` after the change.
claims.why: The function returns exactly that tuple, as shown in the code.

claims.text: PRECEDENCE, and it is deliberate: could_not_run  >  regressed  >  not_fixed  >  fixed
claims.why: The code checks unknown first, then regressed, then unfixed, then fixed – exactly that order.

claims.text: ``could_not_run`` first, because an unattributed node is an unknown and an unknown must never be read as a verdict.
claims.why: The code returns OUTCOME_COULD_NOT_RUN if any node status is in NO_VERDICT, before any other checks.

claims.text: ``regressed`` next, because a change that breaks the regression set is reported as breaking it EVEN IF it also turned every FAIL_TO_PASS green -- collapsing those two into one boolean is exactly how a plausible-looking bad patch gets promoted.
claims.why: The code checks regressed before unfixed; if regressed is non-empty it returns OUTCOME_REGRESSED without considering unfixed.

claims.text: Takes the frozen :class:`Selection`, NOT the task dict, and that is the structural half of the immutability rule: once a selection is frozen there is no code path left that can consult the task for node ids again, so a task mutated mid-evaluation (by a runner, a gate, or a caller holding the same dict) cannot change what is measured.
claims.why: The claim about immutability and no code path consulting the task is a design statement. The code takes a Selection and does not use task, but other parts of the system are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Two invocations on purpose: a collection error in one list must not turn the other list into ``not_run`` (measured -- one uncollectable node id aborts the whole invocation with exit 4 and nothing else runs).
claims.why: The behavior of runner() on error (exit 4) is not defined in this chunk. The code does separate invocations but the error handling is not shown.

observations.what: CorrectnessResult.to_dict() converts after_f2p and after_p2p to sorted dicts, fixed_nodes/unfixed_nodes/regressed_nodes to lists, and duration_s to rounded float.
judge_after_state constructs unknown by merging after_f2p and after_p2p keys, then checking if any status is in NO_VERDICT. NO_VERDICT is not defined in this chunk.
_run_lists appends f2p_run.to_dict() to runs unconditionally, but p2p_run.to_dict() is appended only if selection.pass_to_pass is non-empty. This asymmetry may be intentional.
evaluate_change is incomplete; its body starts after the shown code. The function signature includes patch_bytes: bytes | None = None.
